newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airline stocks up as fuel prices drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airline stocks up as fuel prices drop.

text.p: U.S. airline stocks jumped Thursday as jet fuel prices declined after a fiscal quarter of rising costs.

Jet fuel prices, which are pegged to the price of heating oil, have tumbled about $0.0525 a gallon in the last two days to about $0.714 a gallon in New York Harbor and about $0.695 a gallon in the Gulf Coast.
Airline stocks have been under pressure lately as many carriers issued warnings that their third quarter results may be dampened by higher jet fuel costs.
Airline analysts also caution that airlines' third quarter earnings - expected next week - will be clouded by charges from a legal settlement with travel agents and fare fluctuations.
The biggest gainers of the day included AMR Corp, which jumped 2-3/4 to 85-3/8, UAL Corp, which increased 1-1/2 to 45 and Delta Air Lines Inc, up 1 to 69-3/4.

AMR's stock also gained as the company's chief executive Robert Crandall said Thursday he expected the carrier to report "decent" fourth quarter profits despite continuing cost pressures due to jet fuel prices.
